title: Statistics Cheat Sheet
question: What is the statistical toolkit for environmental and mining data, from exploratory analysis, trends, extremes and spatial statistics to assay QA/QC, geostatistics, sampling theory, reliability, project economics and censored water-quality inference, applied to real observations with the assumptions, the reading of the output and the pitfalls written down?
one_liner: Runnable, annotated analysis scripts, each printing an interpretation of what it computed, condensed into a one-page method chooser.
aim: Document the statistical toolkit for environmental and mining data as runnable, annotated examples on real or clearly labelled synthetic data, with assumptions, interpretation and failure modes stated for each method.
scope: General methods on climate, river and station data: exploratory analysis, hypothesis tests, regression, time series, trend and change-point detection, extremes, resampling, multivariate and spatial methods, Bayesian estimation and machine learning. Methods specific to mining practice: assay exploratory analysis and capping, compositional data, QA/QC, geostatistics, sampling theory, equipment reliability, safety rates, project economics, environmental monitoring, and inference with non-detects: seasonal Kendall, Gehan, censored regression, ProUCL-style upper confidence limits, prediction and tolerance limits.
conclusion: Runnable reference with generated worked-example results; no new scientific study is claimed.

summary.question: Worked examples of the statistics used on environmental and mining data, each run on real observations or clearly labelled synthetic data with its assumptions and pitfalls written out.

finding: Each script applies one family of methods to real or clearly labelled synthetic data and prints an interpretation, so the output reads like a worked example. The cheat sheet is the index: a table from question to method to script section, with the assumptions and the failure modes beside each.

traps.how: Station-temperature interpolation uses leave-one-out validation with the trend and variograms fitted inside each fold. Transfer to an unsampled region requires a separate spatial holdout.
The hypothesis-test section covers multiple comparisons and false-discovery control; the censored-inference section applies Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg to pairwise era comparisons.
Values below detection are handled by Kaplan-Meier and ROS for summaries and by Gehan, censored MLE and Akritas-Theil-Sen for tests and trends, never by substitution.
Compositional data: percentages and ppm are closed, so log-ratio transforms precede biplots and models.
Lab bias and precision are measured with CRM control charts, CUSUM and duplicate analysis before assays are trusted.
Declustering corrects the preferential-sampling bias of drilling where the grade is high.

figures.caption: Regression kriging and residual uncertainty; the station-elevation grid is approximate.
Residual variogram fitted to station climatologies.
Estimates compared with exhaustive block truth; the uncertainty panel shows mean point variance, not block-estimate uncertainty.
Seeded synthetic certified-reference-material controls and planted laboratory bias.
Seasonal Kendall on flow-adjusted copper: the within-month series the test compares, and the per-month Sen slopes agreeing in sign.

not_claimed: A reference, not a study; no new empirical finding is claimed.
data: NOAA CO2, GISTEMP, GHCN-Daily, USGS streamflow and station climatologies
Public and synthetic assay, duplicate, variogram, reliability, safety, price and water-quality datasets
